title: Egg Omelet with Meat and Tomatoes

content.title: About
content.content: An egg omelet or scrambled eggs with added meat and tomatoes is a nutritious dish often enjoyed for breakfast or a light dinner. Eggs provide high‑quality protein, meat adds extra iron and B‑vitamins, and tomatoes contribute fresh flavor and lycopene.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Tomatoes are rich in lycopene, an antioxidant that enhances cellular protection.
Combining eggs with meat increases the bioavailability of iron compared to eating them separately.
Omelets are easily adapted to dietary needs: lean cuts of meat or turkey can be used instead of fattier options.
The tradition of adding fillings to omelets exists worldwide—from French "omelette aux fines herbes" to Mexican "huevos revueltos con chorizo".

items.title: High‑quality protein
items.content: Eggs and meat together supply all essential amino acids, supporting muscle growth and tissue repair.

items.title: Rich in B‑vitamins
items.content: Vitamin B12 and B6 from meat and eggs support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Lycopene and antioxidants
items.content: Tomatoes provide lycopene, which may help reduce the risk of cardiovascular disease.

items.title: Immune support
items.content: Vitamin D from eggs and zinc from meat contribute to a healthy immune response.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: The blend of protein and moderate fat delivers lasting satiety and steady energy.

items.title: Saturated fat content
items.content: Meat can be a source of saturated fat; choose lean cuts or limit the portion size.

items.title: Egg allergy
items.content: Some individuals are allergic to eggs and should avoid this dish.

items.title: Cholesterol levels
items.content: Eggs contain cholesterol; people with high cholesterol should consume them in moderation.

items.title: Foodborne illness
items.content: Meat must be fully cooked to prevent salmonella and other bacterial risks.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Beat the eggs, stir in diced cooked or lean meat and chopped tomatoes, then cook in a lightly oiled pan until set to your liking. Serve hot, optionally garnished with fresh herbs.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Best enjoyed fresh. If needed, store leftovers in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 24 hours. Reheat thoroughly to an internal temperature of 75 °C before serving.
